title: An additive tensor equivalence preserves derived tensor with a degree-zero module
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ and $(\mathcal D,K)$ be sites essentially small in the same coefficient universe $r$ [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ and $S$ be sheaves of commutative rings in that universe. Use the categories $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] in independent localization universes, and the published K-flat derived tensors [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Suppose $F:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ is an additive equivalence supplied with a natural isomorphism $F(A\otimes_R B)\cong F(A)\otimes_S F(B)$ for ordinary sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For every $X\in D(R)$ and $N\in\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ there exists an isomorphism
$$D(F)(X\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N[0])\cong D(F)(X)\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}F(N)[0],$$
where $N[0]$ is the module in cohomological degree zero and $D(F)$ is exact termwise derived transport [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. No boundedness, flatness of $N$, nonzero-ring or inhabited-site assumption is required.

source.place: definition-K-flat, lemma-K-flat-resolution and definition-derived-tor (Tags 06YN, 06YS and 06YU); exact-equivalence step in lem-sf-clopen-preserves-residue-tor.

proof.text: An additive equivalence and its inverse preserve homology and all coproducts. Curry the supplied ordinary tensor natural isomorphism and use the total-complex mapBifunctorComparison to obtain F(Tot(P,Q)) isomorphic to Tot(F(P),F(Q)). This applies without boundedness because an equivalence preserves the direct sums in each degree.

If P is K-flat and Z is acyclic on the target site, F inverse(Z) is acyclic. Tensor this complex with P, apply exact F, and use the total comparison followed by the counit F(F inverse(Z)) isomorphic to Z. The result Tot(Z,F(P)) is acyclic. Therefore F(P) is K-flat.

Choose a representative Y for X and a K-flat resolution P to Y. Apply the single-tensor comparison on both sites to compute Q(P) tensor N[0] and Q(F(P)) tensor F(N)[0] by their termwise tensor complexes. The ordinary comparison c(P^q,N) is a chain isomorphism between F of the first complex and the second, by naturality for (d_P,id_N). Localize it, use the exact-functor localization comparison, and transport along Q(P) isomorphic to X. Their composite is the required isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06YN, 06YS and 06YU. Apply the definition of K-flatness through an exact tensor equivalence and use the existing single-tensor comparison; no full derived monoidal coherence theorem is required.

theorem ringedEquivalence_derivedTensorComparison
    {C : Type c} [Category.{h} C] [EssentiallySmall.{r} C]
    {D : Type d} [Category.{k} D] [EssentiallySmall.{r} D]
    {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {K : GrothendieckTopology D}
    (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}) (S : Sheaf K CommRingCat.{r})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ringedSiteModules.{r}
      ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (ringedSiteModules.{r}
      ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj S))]
    (F : ringedSiteModules.{r}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R) ⥤
      ringedSiteModules.{r}
        ((sheafCompose K (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj S))
    [F.Additive] [F.IsEquivalence]
    (c₀ : tensor _ ⋙ F ≅ F.prod F ⋙ tensor _) :
    ∀ (X : DerivedCategory (ringedSiteModules.{r}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R)))
      (N : ringedSiteModules.{r}
        ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R)),
      Nonempty (F.mapDerivedCategory.obj
          ((siteDerivedTensorIndependentCoefficients J R).obj
            (X, (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj N)) ≅
        (siteDerivedTensorIndependentCoefficients K S).obj
          (F.mapDerivedCategory.obj X, (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj (F.obj N)))
